subject: Narrow overlap — propose rotating-host demo windows for Acme Health
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.ai>
To: Rebecca Moore <rebecca@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 10 Jul 2026 13:12:00 -0400
Subject: Narrow overlap — propose rotating-host demo windows for Acme Health

Hi Rebecca —

Thanks again for the interest and for sharing the list of use cases. Based on the team sync this morning I wanted to get ahead of scheduling: your product + our engineering demos are going to require a ~60–90 min deep-dive, and we noticed the overlap window between your East Coast team and our EU engineers is fairly tight.

Quick context: during Northern Hemisphere summer the overlap is roughly 8:00–11:00 ET / 14:00–17:00 CEST. That gives a few solid hours but still makes it hard to pull in senior EU folks after 16:00 CEST when their core day ends. We want to avoid repeating the situation where we ask engineers to join at 19:00 local.

Proposed approach (lightweight rotation):
- Option A: Single full-run during your morning (8:30 ET / 14:30 CEST) with EU engineering leading the demo and US PMs joining — good for deep technical Q&A.
- Option B: Shorter 45-min demo at 10:00 ET / 16:00 CEST (concise walkthrough + recording + follow-up deep dive with SREs) — good if you want multiple stakeholder-friendly slots.
- Option C: Two-week rotating cadence: Week 1 EU-hosted at 14:00 CEST, Week 2 US-friendly recap at 09:00 ET (recorded); minimizes late-evening requests for either team.

I've attached a proposed .ics with candidate slots (proposed_slots.ics) and a draft agenda (demo_agenda_v2.pdf). Can you tell us which option you'd prefer and which stakeholders must be present? If none of the listed slots work, please reply with best 2-hour windows on your side and we'll map to EU availability.

Note: small DST nuance — in late Oct the EU->US DST offset shifts and will temporarily reduce the overlap by an hour for ~2 weeks; we'll put a calendar guardrail around that period if we lock in a multi-week cadence.

Thanks —
Jordan Blake
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
jordan@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0192

Attachments: proposed_slots.ics (calendar options), demo_agenda_v2.pdf (draft)
From: Rebecca Moore <rebecca@acmehealth.com>

Date: Mon, 13 Jul 2026 09:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Narrow overlap — propose rotating-host demo windows for Acme Health

On Fri, Jul 10, 2026 at 1:12 PM Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Thanks again for the interest and for sharing the list of use cases.

Thanks Jordan — this is very helpful context. Our engineering and product folks are available most mornings ET; 8:30–10:30 ET is ideal. I previewed the .ics and 14:30 CEST/8:30 ET looks good for the core group.

Two quick asks: can we keep the demo to 60 minutes (we have back-to-back committees) and make sure there's a dedicated 15-minute SRE follow-up window with an EU engineer if deep infra questions come up? Also, please include a short pre-read 24 hrs before.

Rebecca Moore
Product Lead, Integrations — Acme Health
rebecca@acmehealth.com

From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rebecca Moore <rebecca@acmehealth.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 14:05:00 +02:00
Subject: Re: Narrow overlap — propose rotating-host demo windows for Acme Health

Thanks for looping us in. 14:30 CEST is within EU core hours for our infra team — they can lead the live demo. A few operational notes from engineering:

- We can keep the session to 60 minutes if the agenda reserves 25–30 minutes for live demo + 20–25 for Q&A. If heavy infra topics come up we should automatically slot the 15-min SRE follow-up (as Rebecca suggested).
- Please share any sensitive test data requirements ahead of time; we prefer sanitized samples (PII redacted) for recorded sessions.
- If the session runs late, our fallback is to hand the remaining infra questions to a recorded deep-dive + 30-min technical office hours the next EU morning.

Also a quick DST flag: when EU reverts in late Oct the overlap shortens briefly — if we agree on a multi-week rotation we should include a calendar note and switch to Option B timings that week.

Soojín (she/her)
Senior Backend Engineer — Redwood Inference
soojin@redwood.ai

Great — thanks Rebecca and Soojin.

Plan good to go:
- Confirmed 60-min demo: 14:30 CEST / 08:30 ET on Thu, 2026-07-22 (EU hosts lead).
- 15-min SRE follow-up reserved immediately after the demo; Marcus will be the backup.
- I'll publish the pre-read by Tue 2026-07-20 and attach the recording + infra office hours link after the session.
- We'll add a calendar note for the Oct DST edge-case and automatically propose Option B timings for that week if a conflict appears.

Calendar event: https://calendar.google.com/event?eid=acme-demo-20260714 (invite sent).

Thanks — looking forward to it.
